sources.claims_supported: Octopus agreed the sale of Shell Energy Broadband to TalkTalk shareholders on 6 February 2024; TalkTalk already supported the service platform; customers were to be contacted during migration.
Shell Energy's current support result states that broadband and phone customers have moved to TalkTalk.

Approximately 500,000 customers were transferred, migration was automatic, contracts and routers continued during the move, and customers should not cancel payment instructions without checking their account.
Ofcom fined Shell Energy £1.4 million in November 2023 for failures involving end-of-contract and annual best-tariff notifications affecting more than 70,000 customers.
Under One Touch Switch, a new provider generally arranges the switch and the old service ends when the new one is working; customers should check provider-hosted email consequences.
Historical service-quality context: Shell Energy recorded 31 broadband complaints per 100,000 customers in Q2 2022 against an industry average of 11; this is not a current TalkTalk measure.

research_summary: The natural UK query is 'Shell Energy broadband'; the duplicated final word in the packet appears to be a keyword-data artefact and is retained only as the validator's primary_keyword value. Current results mix obsolete commercial reviews with accurate archive pages. The official Octopus announcement and current Shell support result establish that the broadband customer base moved to TalkTalk in 2024. The page should therefore be an archive and support guide, not a live deal page. Ranking pages commonly use 1,300 to 2,000 words, contents-style scanning, package facts, speed and router sections, pros and cons, comparisons and FAQs. The most useful differentiator is a prominent current-status answer backed by official and regulatory evidence.
depth_rationale: A 1,500-word minimum matches the accurate Selectra archive and exceeds the roughly 1,300-word Broadbandswitch review without padding to the longest result. That depth is needed to answer both major intents visible in the results: prospective users checking whether Shell deals still exist and former customers seeking TalkTalk, billing, router, complaint or switching help. Historical package details are included only where they help identify a legacy service, while current actions and limitations receive more space.
